summary: Molot's northern march: the margravate, the fortress line, the balance between Sonargur and Parim, the march economy, and the march at war.

margraves_house.name: The Margrave's House
margraves_house.desc: The margraves of Molot have held the northern march for generations, and balanced Lerendor by courting Parim whenever Sonargur grew too strong. The house is old, and it is canny.

margraves_house_2.name: The Margrave's Word
margraves_house_2.desc: When the Margrave speaks, the march listens. His word is law in the towers and honoured in the villages, and nobody in Molot would think of breaking it.

iron_discipline_spirit.name: Iron Discipline
iron_discipline_spirit.desc: A garrison that breaks its ranks is flogged, and a garrison that holds is fed. The march lords keep both rules strictly, and the men do not complain.

garrison_drill_spirit.name: Garrison Drill
garrison_drill_spirit.desc: Every tower has a drill-yard and every drill-yard has a master. The garrisons of Molot practise the defence of a wall until they can do it blindfold.

garrison_drill_2.name: The Iron March
garrison_drill_2.desc: The garrisons of the march are the best drilled in the North after Lerendor's own. They hold a wall like a mountain and fall back like a tide.

watch_fires.name: The Watch-Fires
watch_fires.desc: A line of watch-fires runs the length of the northern march, each tower within sight of the next. A warning at one end of Molot reaches the other before the horn has stopped.

march_mercenaries.name: Swords for Hire
march_mercenaries.desc: Molot lets its spare swords to anyone who pays. The march lords take a tenth and ask no questions, and the veterans learn a great deal.

balance_of_the_north.name: The Balance of the North
balance_of_the_north.desc: Molot plays Sonargur and Parim one against the other, with a smile and a fine sense of timing. Both courts compete for its friendship, and neither is quite sure of it.

march_herds.name: Herds of the March
march_herds.desc: The march is poor in grain and rich in herds. Shaggy cattle and sheep graze on the moor behind the towers, and feed the garrisons all winter.

march_at_war.name: The March at War
march_at_war.desc: The towers are manned, the beacons are laid and the garrisons are provisioned for a siege. The Margrave has let it be known that the march will not give way.

chapels_of_the_march.title: Chapels of the March
chapels_of_the_march.desc: The almoners of the Houses of the First Light have asked leave to build chapels in the towers of the march. They would tend the sick, keep a granary and bless the watch. The Margrave's captains say the march needs soldiers, not priests, but the garrisons are not so sure.

options.name: The march needs soldiers, not priests

molot_envoys.title: Envoys from the March
molot_envoys.desc: A herald in the grey cloak of the northern march has presented himself at court. Margrave Wokla sends greetings and a gift of drilled spearmen's songs, and hopes that the court will remember Molot when it counts its friends. He has said the same to the other court.

molot_offers_the_march.title: Molot Offers the March
molot_offers_the_march.desc: Margrave Wokla writes to Parim from the northern march. Molot's towers, its garrisons and its watch-fires are at the king's disposal, he says, as long as the king will guarantee the march. The offer is formal and the letter is short.

focuses.name: The Margravate
focuses.desc: Molot is the northern march: two states of towers and garrisons whose watch-fires look over cold water. Margrave Wokla is a soldier at peace, and likes the peace because it lets him choose his friends.

focuses.name: The March Lords
focuses.desc: The lords of the march each hold a tower and its lands, in return for a garrison and a share of the watch. They meet at the Margrave's table each quarter, with their swords at their sides.

focuses.name: The Margrave's Court
focuses.desc: The Margrave holds court in the largest tower, with a clerk, a herald and a chaplain at his side. It is the only court in the North where the king sits closest to the door.

focuses.name: Iron Discipline
focuses.desc: The garrisons of the march are drilled with an iron hand. A garrison that holds is fed, and one that breaks is flogged, and the rules are read aloud at every dawn.

focuses.name: Chapels of the March
focuses.desc: The almoners ask for chapels in the towers of the march. The captains are suspicious, and the garrisons are interested.

focuses.name: The Margrave's Word
focuses.desc: Margrave Wokla's word is law from the sea to the moors. A lord who disputes it answers to the Margrave himself, in his own hall.

focuses.name: Molot Stands Alone
focuses.desc: Molot is small, but it is not easily moved. The Margrave stands on his highest tower and proclaims that the march will stand alone, and will fall to nobody.

focuses.name: The March Fortresses
focuses.desc: The great fortress at the heart of the march is rebuilt in grey stone, with a double wall and a deep ditch. It is the keep of Molot, and it will not fall.

focuses.name: The Northern Towers
focuses.desc: A string of towers is built along the northern ridge, each within a mile of the next. The garrisons are small, but the beacons are large.

focuses.name: Garrison Drill
focuses.desc: Each tower has a drill-yard and each drill-yard has a master. The garrisons practise the defence of a wall until they can do it blindfold.

focuses.name: Sea Forts
focuses.desc: Forts are built on the cliffs above the northern water, with stone walls, sea-gates and a beacon on the highest tower. They guard the coast and warn the march.

focuses.name: The Watch-Fires
focuses.desc: A chain of watch-fires is laid along the whole of the march, each stack of wood tended by a family of the village. A light at one end of Molot is seen at the other within the hour.

focuses.name: March Engineers
focuses.desc: Master builders and stone-cutters are brought into the Margrave's service. They build walls, siege-engines and covered ways, and teach the garrisons to use them.

focuses.name: The Long Garrison
focuses.desc: A standing garrison is kept in each coastal fort, and relieved by the villages in turn. Molot has more men under arms than it can easily feed, and means to keep them there.

focuses.name: The Iron March
focuses.desc: The march is a single chain of towers, forts and watch-fires, under a single command. Whoever comes against it comes against the whole of it.

focuses.name: The Balance of the North
focuses.desc: Molot sits between Sonargur and Parim, and has no wish to be anyone's subject. The Margrave writes down what he is prepared to give, and what he would like in return.

focuses.name: Envoys to Sonargur
focuses.desc: A herald in the grey cloak of the march is sent to the crown at Sonargur. He carries a gift of drilled spearmen, and a plain request for friendship.

focuses.name: Envoys to Parim
focuses.desc: A second herald is sent south to the king in Parim, with the same gifts and the same request. The two heralds do not meet, by arrangement.

focuses.name: Swords for Hire
focuses.desc: Molot's spare swords are let out to whoever pays. The Margrave takes a tenth and the veterans take a lesson, and nobody in the march complains.

focuses.name: Play One Against the Other
focuses.desc: Molot makes its friendship available to each court in turn. Sonargur and Parim bid against one another, and the Margrave names the price.

focuses.name: An Oath to Sonargur
focuses.desc: The Margrave kneels to the crown at Sonargur, and swears an oath on a bare blade. It is a hard thing for a march lord to do, and he does it in silence.

focuses.name: The Balance Holds
focuses.desc: Molot has kept its balance for a generation, and the Margrave means to keep it for another. The two courts do not love him, but both are careful of him.

focuses.name: The March Economy
focuses.desc: The march is poor, and the Margrave wants it less so. He builds workshops in the shelter of the towers, and sets the garrison to learn a trade.

focuses.name: Armouries of Molot
focuses.desc: A great armoury is raised beside the Margrave's keep. Smiths from the border towns forge spears, mail and shield-bosses, and the garrison carries what they make.

focuses.name: March Roads
focuses.desc: A paved road is run the length of the march, from tower to tower and from tower to coast. The garrisons can move in a day what used to take three.

focuses.name: Herds of the March
focuses.desc: Shaggy cattle and moor sheep graze behind the towers. They feed the garrisons in winter and clothe them in summer.

focuses.name: March Provisions
focuses.desc: Grain is carted in from the south and stored in the stone cellars of the towers. A garrison with a year's bread can stand a year's siege.

focuses.name: The March Holds
focuses.desc: The beacons are lit along the whole of the march, and the Margrave calls his lords to the keep. The march will not give way, and it says so aloud.

focuses.name: Fire the Beacons
focuses.desc: Black hulls have been seen off the northern cliffs. The beacons are lit, the sea-forts are manned and the garrisons are woken.

focuses.name: The March Stands Apart
focuses.desc: Lerendor has left the old treaty, and Molot does not follow. The Margrave declares the march to be its own master, standing with the North, and with nobody else.

focuses.name: The March with Parim
focuses.desc: Margrave Wokla remembers the old alliance, and sends word to Parim that Molot will keep it. His garrisons are offered, and his towers.

focuses.name: March Companies with the Heir
focuses.desc: The Heir has returned, and the march sends a company of its best to join him. The Margrave stays behind with the rest, and holds the towers.

focuses.name: The Watch Ends
focuses.desc: The watch-fires burn low at last. The garrisons go home, and the Margrave takes off his helm for the first time in a year.
